questions.q: What question did Jesus ask Bartimaeus in Mark 10:51, and why does the chapter highlight it?
options: "Do you believe I can do this?" — to test his faith
"What do you want me to do for you?" — it required him to name his desire plainly in Jesus' hearing
"Why are you shouting?" — to quieten the crowd
"Who told you about me?" — to check his source
questions.explanation: Everyone could see Bartimaeus was blind, but Jesus asked anyway. The same question to James and John (Mark 10:36) exposed a very different desire. Saying what we want tells us the truth about ourselves.

questions.q: What does the chapter call the first mistake in setting an intention?
options: Arriving with too much: a project charter of things to fix
Having no expectations at all
Sharing the intention with someone else
Writing it down instead of praying it
questions.explanation: Psalm 27:4 models the alternative: 'One thing have I asked of the LORD.' David gathered his desire into the one that lay underneath the others.

questions.q: Which is an example of an open-handed intention rather than an outcome-focused expectation?
options: "God must tell me whether to leave my job."
"I must forgive everything by Sunday."
"I want to remain present with God and truthful about the distance I feel."
"This retreat must cure my burnout."
questions.explanation: An intention is a request, not a demand. It gives you a place to begin while leaving God free to redirect your attention.

questions.q: Why does the chapter point to Hannah in 1 Samuel 1?
options: She fasted before praying
She brought her anguish before God without disguising it, an example of unpolished honesty
She wrote her prayer down
Eli praised her for her eloquence
questions.explanation: Eli assumed she was drunk. Scripture does not reward polished prayers; a hollow but correct-sounding intention can be a way of avoiding the retreat before it starts.

questions.q: What does the chapter say about hidden intentions, such as hoping God will confirm a decision already made?
options: They disqualify you from the retreat
They should be ignored
They should be named and brought to God, because left unspoken they can distort what you hear
They are always sinful
questions.explanation: If you seek only confirmation, you may read every impression as confirmation. Psalm 139:23–24 is the prayer for this: 'Search me, O God, and know my heart.'

questions.q: What does 'open hands' NOT mean, according to the chapter?
options: Leaving the outcome with God
Refusing to manipulate the retreat into your preferred answer
Passivity toward abuse, injustice, danger, or responsibilities that require action
Being willing to receive peace instead of an answer
questions.explanation: Surrender means not forcing the retreat to produce your answer. It does not mean surrendering wisdom, boundaries or safety.

reflection: What I am carrying: in a few sentences, the situation you are coming from.
What I am asking: one sentence, in the first person, addressed to God. Plain words.
What I have not said: the hidden hope or fear, if there is one.
What I am releasing: one sentence surrendering your demand for a particular retreat outcome.
